article.title: NFL EDGE Sunday Morning Brief
article.dek: The nor'easter is still sitting on the Giants game, the 6am board deals a new set of cards, and the Bears' Monday-night quarterback question finally has an answer.

items.headline: The nor'easter is still parked on the Hit Rate card
paragraphs: Titans at Giants, 1 p.m. ET (11 a.m. MDT) at MetLife. Final forecast: rain through the whole game, low 60s, northeast wind 16 to 23 mph with gusts as high as 39 mph, and a 90% chance of precipitation. The winds are a touch lighter than Saturday's call (gusts were 41), but it is the same storm.

This is the game on the app's Hit Rate card — and this morning, the Balanced card too. Both are Giants moneyline at -130 on DraftKings. The -130 means every $1.30 you risk wins $1. Terry's model says the Giants win about 64 times in 100; the price implies about 57. The app grades it LOW confidence and negative expected value.

The weather doesn't change the app's number. It changes how the game is played — wet ball, kicking adventure, running game. The market's read on the storm is the price: it went from -135 Saturday morning to -140 on one book Saturday afternoon, then back to -130 on DraftKings this morning (FanDuel shows -138). The storm was priced in early. Nobody is panic-buying it now.
items.takeaway: Same storm, same card, slightly cheaper price than last night.

items.headline: Sunday's injury and quarterback news, all in one place
paragraphs: Chicago (Monday night): Caleb Williams (hamstring) is OUT — he didn't practice all week. Tyson Bagent cleared the concussion protocol Saturday, practiced in full, and head coach Ben Johnson says he'll be available. Bagent is officially questionable, but he's the expected starter, and the app agrees: its expected starter for the Bears is Tyson Bagent. If anything changes before Monday, 38-year-old Case Keenum — who hasn't played since 2023 — is the fallback.
Philadelphia (Monday night): tight end Dallas Goedert (knee), receiver Marquise Brown (ankle), and tackle Fred Johnson (knee) are all OUT. Linebacker Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) is questionable.
Seattle: Sam Darnold is expected to start, and the app's expected starter matches. Safeties Julian Love and Ty Okada are both OUT — that news broke Friday night.

Washington: Marcus Mariota starts for Jayden Daniels — the app shows Mariota. Giants: Jameis Winston starts for Jaxson Dart — the app shows Winston. Tennessee: Cam Ward is the starter — the app shows Ward. No surprises anywhere. The app has caught up on every quarterback.

Rio (Ravens at Cowboys, 2:25 p.m. MDT): Zay Flowers remains the game-time call. Inactive lists come out 90 minutes before kickoff — about 12:55 p.m. MDT for this one — so the morning board can't have them. That's the one to watch.
items.takeaway: The quarterbacks are settled and the app matches on all of them. The only real game-time call is Flowers in Rio.

items.headline: Weather everywhere else: one more game to watch
paragraphs: Seahawks at Commanders in Landover (1 p.m. ET) is the only other game on the radar: about a 43–44% chance of light rain and northwest wind building toward 15 mph, mid-60s. Worth knowing, not worth building around.

The rest is clean. Rio is overcast but dry at 71 for Ravens-Cowboys. Sunday night in Denver is 82 and mostly cloudy for Rams-Broncos. Buffalo, Cleveland, Cincinnati, Tampa, Jacksonville, Miami, and Santa Clara all check out fine.
items.takeaway: Two games have weather. One of them has a nor'easter.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: What the three cards actually say this morning
paragraphs: The board refreshed at 6 a.m., so these are new numbers. Hit Rate and Balanced are the same pick this morning: Giants moneyline at -130 on DraftKings.

Hit Rate asks “which supported pick looks most likely to win?” It forgoes value for win probability — the app's own tutorial says “Hit Rate ≠ Profit Rate.” Balanced asks for “a strong pick without paying too much” — the middle ground, a good starting point for a new bettor. This morning both questions landed on the same answer. The -130 means every $1.30 you risk wins $1. Terry's model says the Giants win about 64 times in 100; the price implies about 57. The app grades it LOW confidence and negative expected value (about -5%). Neither card is pretending to be a value play, and that's fine — that's not the question they answer.

Value is the model's +EV play, always: Raiders moneyline at +164 on DraftKings at New Orleans. The +164 means every $1 you risk wins $1.64. The model says Las Vegas wins about 38 times in 100; the price implies about 38. This is the only one of the three the app prices at positive expected value (about +0.4%), with MEDIUM reliability.

One honest note: the model's Giants number cooled overnight — yesterday morning it said about 73 in 100. Same pick, smaller enthusiasm. And for your actual stake, the app does the math for you from your bankroll and staking setting, and it's deliberately conservative. Unit numbers are the app's sizing language, not a dollar instruction.
items.takeaway: Three cards, two picks. Read the question each card is answering before you read the pick.

items.headline: How to use the storm news with the app
paragraphs: News first, app second. The nor'easter is real news. Here's how to actually use it.

The weather doesn't rewrite the app's number — the model priced the teams, not the clouds. What weather CAN do is move the market: if bettors pile onto a side because of the storm, the price moves, and the price is what you pay. So the move to watch is the Giants' price, not the rain gauge. Overnight it moved the wrong way for storm-buyers: -135 down to -130 on DraftKings.

And if your book isn't DraftKings or FanDuel, or it shows a different number than the app's board, you don't have to guess. Tap Check in the app, type in YOUR book's line and price, and the app runs it back through Terry's model and the evaluator and gives you a bet-or-no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: The app's number is the anchor. Your book's price is the decision. Check bridges them.

items.headline: Sunday morning board: what moved overnight
paragraphs: Titans at Giants: spread steady at Giants -2.5, total steady at 37.5. A day and a half of nor'easter headlines has moved the spread and total nowhere — the storm was priced in early. The only flicker is the moneyline: -135 Saturday morning, -140 on one book Saturday afternoon, -130 on DraftKings this morning (-138 on FanDuel). A slight buyback, not a trend.

Seahawks at Commanders: the mover. Seattle went from -7.5 to -8.5 on DraftKings overnight; the total sits at 40.5. The market kept buying Seattle after the Darnold confirmation and with both starting safeties ruled out. Terry's model has Seattle by 7.74 — the market has now moved PAST the model. The Darnold news is more than fully priced. Don't chase -8.5 on the old thesis.

Chiefs at Dolphins: Kansas City -10.5 to -10, total 45 to 45.5. A small drift toward Miami. The model sees Kansas City by only about 4 — still the widest model-market disagreement on the board, and the market hasn't moved toward it at all.

Ravens at Cowboys (Rio): still Baltimore -3.5, total 53.5. The model sees Dallas by 1.5. Five points of disagreement in a strange stadium, and more than 24 hours of injury news hasn't moved the market a tick. A reason to study, not a reason to bet Dallas.

Eagles at Bears (Monday): Philadelphia -3.5, total 42.5. The quarterback wildcard is resolved — Bagent is the app's expected starter. The model has Chicago by 1.8, a five-plus-point disagreement with the market on Monday night. That's a study note, not a bet slip: backup quarterback, Monday night, strange spot.

The board refreshes at 6 a.m. and 6 p.m. Denver. Inactives land 90 minutes before kickoff, so the morning board can't have them — the Rio game-time call on Flowers is the one that could move a number this afternoon.
items.takeaway: Seattle is the only real overnight move, and it moved past the model. Everything else is holding.

items.headline: Sunday morning, in this order
paragraphs: Three things to re-check before the early games. First, inactive lists 90 minutes before kickoff — the Rio game (2:25 p.m. MDT) is the one with a real game-time call in Zay Flowers, so check around 12:55 p.m. MDT. Second, one last MetLife forecast check: the heaviest rain is currently timed for the second half (3–6 p.m. ET), so rain timing decides how ugly that game gets. Third, if you like a number that moved overnight — Seattle at -8.5 is the candidate — run YOUR book's price through Check before deciding anything. The board is a snapshot. Your price is the decision.
items.takeaway: Inactives, then the sky, then Check. In that order.

items.headline: Betting term of the day: handle
paragraphs: Handle is the total DOLLARS bet on a side. Tickets are the NUMBER of bets. They're different, and the difference matters.

Say 70% of the tickets are on the Giants but only 40% of the handle. That means the average Giants bet is small and the average Titans bet is big — a few large wagers outweighing a crowd of small ones. That tickets-vs-handle split is exactly what the Fade watches for: heavy public tickets on one side, heavier money on the other.

This morning there's no verified split worth writing up — I checked VSiN's board and the splits pages didn't have usable ticket/handle numbers — so there's no Fade today. The section stays empty rather than forcing one.
items.takeaway: Tickets count heads. Handle counts dollars. The Fade watches the gap between them.
